Web Projects

Build a local four-file website with styles, behavior and data—then inspect the result.

IN THIS CHAPTER

All 19 chapters →

What you will learn

  • Connect HTML, CSS, JavaScript and JSON using relative paths.
  • Use preview, live save and the console to diagnose mistakes.

Before you begin

Chapter 6 project skills and Chapter 12 loopback/LAN concepts. Static HTML preview needs no Linux userland download.

Create the workspace

Projects → + → New Project → Static Web creates index.html. Name the project PhonePage. Open the whole project in the Editor, then add style.css, app.js and data.json in the same root. Replace the template with the four complete files below.

No remote libraries, fonts or images are required. The JavaScript fetches a sibling JSON file, not a public API. Keep the filenames and their case exact.

The four files

index.html

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My phone-made page</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
  <script src="app.js" defer></script>
</head>
<body>
  <h1 id="name">My page</h1>
  <p id="bio">Loading local data…</p>
  <button id="count" type="button">Clicks: 0</button>
</body>
</html>

style.css

:root { --accent: #3ddc84; }
body { margin: 2rem auto; padding: 1rem; max-width: 40rem;
       background: #101713; color: #edf2ed; font-family: sans-serif; }
h1 { color: var(--accent); }
button { padding: 1rem; font: inherit; }
button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent); }

app.js

fetch("data.json")
  .then(response => {
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + response.status);
    return response.json();
  })
  .then(data => {
    document.querySelector("#name").textContent = data.name;
    document.querySelector("#bio").textContent = data.bio;
  })
  .catch(error => {
    document.querySelector("#bio").textContent = "Could not load data";
    console.error(error);
  });
let clicks = 0;
document.querySelector("#count").addEventListener("click", event => {
  clicks += 1;
  event.currentTarget.textContent = "Clicks: " + clicks;
});

data.json

{"name":"CodeC learner","bio":"I make small things on my phone."}

RUN opens the local site

Wait for autosave, open index.html and tap RUN. For HTML, this is Web Preview. Expected: “CodeC learner”, the short bio and a button. Tap twice: its label becomes Clicks:2. The exact request origin/port comes from CodeC’s local project server, not a hard-coded URL in these files.

The server exposes project-relative resources so fetch and ES modules work. A file:// fallback may have browser restrictions on fetch/modules; prefer the app’s HTTP preview for this exercise. Plain static files do not universally require a server, but this data-fetching example does.

Make one change at a time

Change --accent in style.css to another readable color, save and watch live reload. If you are still seeing an older state, reload deliberately and confirm the preview belongs to the project you edited. The preview console helps distinguish missing data from a JavaScript exception.

Break data.json temporarily by removing a quote. Expected: the error branch shows “Could not load data” and the console identifies a parse problem. Restore valid JSON; the text should return.

A small module extension

For an optional module exercise, remove the existing app.js script tag and replace it with the tag below. Add message.js and put the import at the top of app.js. Do not include both classic and module versions or you may attach listeners twice.

Replacement HTML script tag

<script type="module" src="app.js"></script>

message.js

export const message = "Module ready";

Add at the top of app.js

import { message } from "./message.js";
console.log(message);

Expected in the local HTTP preview console: Module ready. The ./ is a relative module path, not a package name.

Export locally; share LAN intentionally

Export the project ZIP from Projects and keep all four files together. On another device, enable LAN sharing only for non-sensitive work and use Other devices/QR on the same Wi-Fi. The phone-loopback address is not reachable as your phone from another device. Turn sharing off afterward; this exercise does not publish a public website.

Try it yourself

  1. Change the bio in data.json. Expected: preview updates after save/reload without editing the HTML.
  2. Click the button three times after a fresh load. Expected: Clicks:3.
  3. Add the optional module and check its console message; preserve the four-file version as a known-good backup.

Common mistakes

  • Case or path mismatches can break a linked resource even when index.html opens.
  • Invalid JSON is not a broken compiler. Read the console.
  • Do not use LAN sharing as if it were authentication or public hosting.
